previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prostate cancer undergoing radiation therapy was admitted for acute urinary retention and suspected UTI. He had a similar episode three weeks prior complicated by ESBL Klebsiella infection. On admission, he had suprapubic discomfort, elevated creatinine, and a positive urinalysis. Urine culture confirmed ESBL Klebsiella, and he was treated with ciprofloxacin. He developed C. difficile colitis, likely antibiotic-related, and was started on oral vancomycin. His acute kidney injury, attributed to dehydration, improved with cautious IV hydration. Tacrolimus levels were subtherapeutic and dose was increased. Doxazosin was initiated for urinary retention, and carvedilol was reduced due to overlapping hypotensive effects. He completed scheduled radiation therapy during admission. By discharge, his infection was resolving, renal function had normalized, and he was stable on adjusted medications with follow-up plans.

finished on ___. During that admission, he developed C diff and 
was started on PO vancomycin, which he has been continuing 
currently. It was felt that his urinary retention may be in part 
due to his radiation therapy - doxazosin was added to his 
current tamsulosin in attempt to help his symptoms.  
He noted some difficulty urinating last night as well as loose, 
black stool last night. Also had rigors and chills. Today, he 
was in line at ___ prior to his Radiation appointment 
when he became light headed and faint. He was lowered to the 
floor by bystanders. He did not lose consciousness and says he 
remembers what happened. He returned to the Radiation department

Finger stick was 181. Vitals signs supine were HR 104 BP 137/57,

febrile to 100.4 while in the ED and received acetaminophen 
650mg x1. Labs showed leukocytosis to 13, Cr of 2.3 (baseline

intrathoracic process. Based on prior culture data, he was given 
cefepime. He became febrile to 101 while in the ED and 
progressively more tachycardic and relatively hypotensive 
concerning for developing septic physiology. He was given IVF. A 
repeat lactate in the ED while downstairs returned elevated at 
2.3 from 1.8 several hours earlier. He was given another bolus 
of fluids for 1L, BP rechecked at 130/54.  
On transfer, vitals were: 101.0 122 110/70 20 98%. On the floor, 
he reports generally not feeling well but cannot be more 
specific. Reports some dizziness over the past few days. He 
reports having worsening diarrhea for only the past ___ days 
with ___ loose stools today. His diarrhea had previously 
improved last admission after he started PO vanco. Denies N/V, 
chest pain or SOB. Reports some trouble passing urine which 
started with his radiation, which began ___.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old gentleman with a PMHx ESRD ___ DM/HTN s/p LURT ___, 
CAD, prostate cancer on radiation therapy who was sent to ED 
from radiation oncology after a pre-syncopal episode, found to 
have sepsis secondary to klebsiella UTI.  
 
# Sepsis secondary to UTI: Pt grew GNRs in blood and urine from 
___, was initially covered with cefepime starting ___ but 
then broadened to meropenem due to poor clinical status (AMS, 
fevers). Urine speciated to be klebsiella pneumonia sensitive to 
cefepime which was restarted ___. Continues on cefepime 
(Recieved 1 dose cefepime ___ before changed to meropenem; 
restarted ___.  Daily surviellance blood cultures negative 
since ___. Patient clinically improved, leukocytosis resolved. 
Right sided PICC line was placed and pt was discharged with plan 
to continue cefepime for total 14 day course (day ___.

# LFT elevation: Moderately elevated ALT, AST and alk phos this 
admission. Pt's statin was held and CMV viral load was pending 
at time of discharge. 

# GPC bacteremia: Blood cultures from ___ grew GPCs from one 
bottle. Pt started on IV vancomycin (day ___, Vanco trough 
___ morning 14.9, at goal. Prelim culture results indicate 
coag neg staph. Discontinued vanc per ID, likely contaminant.

# Cdiff infection - Pt was already being treated with PO vanc on 
admission which was continued. Abdominal exam was benign and pt 
denied ongoing diarrhea. He was instructed to continue PO 
vancomycin for 14 days beyong completion of abx course for his 
UTI.

# Pre-syncope - Pt admitted from XRT with presyncopal episode. 
Patient did not lose consciousness, no clear prodromal symptoms 
of chest pain, palpitations, no post-ictal stage. Likely related 
to sepsis, orthostatic on exam ___. Neuro exam non-focal. EKG 
___ showed sinus arrhythmia @ 81bpm, no ST elevations or 
depression, no T wave inversion.  Pt again reported feeling 
dizzy last night, + orthostatics on exam. HCT remained stable 
throughout admission. Likely  due to fluid shift given brisk 
urine output after foley placement (>3L). Pt had no symptoms of 
pre-syncope at time of discharge.

# Prostate Cancer: Currently undergoing XRT M-F. Underwent 2 
sessions of XRT during this admission which he tolerated well. 

# Acute on chronic CKD: Cr of 2.3 on admission. Recent baseline 
of 1.7-1.8. Ultrasound showed hydronephrosis of both native and 
transplanted kidney, likely due to outflow obstruction ___ 
prostate CA. Repeat ultrasound of transplanted kidney ___ 
showed interval improvement of hydronephrosis. Cr at discharge 
had improved to 1.5
  
# Diabetes Mellitus - Had elevated blood sugars in the ED. 
Continued on home regimen of BID lantus + sliding scale humalog. 
FBS 100s-200s for remainder of admission. 

# s/p LURT - ___ DM and HTN. Continued on MMF 500 BID and 
tacrolimus 2.5 mg BID as well as bactrim prophylaxis. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
- Pt discharged with foley catheter. It should be kept in place 
for remainder of radiation therapy. Plan for follow up with 
urology in 2 weeks.
- Discharged with plan to complete 14 day total course of IV 
antibiotics for klebsiella pneumonia UTI and bacteremia
- Pt with recent c diff prior to admission. Pt should continue 
course of PO vanc 14 days beyond cefepime course.
- Home furosemide was discontinued this admission in the setting 
___
